title: October 30, 1909: a boy was born in Bombay who would found both India's top physics institute and its nuclear program.
caption:
October 30, 1909: a boy was born in Bombay who would found both India's top physics institute and its nuclear program.

Educated at Cambridge, he started in mechanical engineering before pivoting to physics - a switch that would reshape India's entire scientific infrastructure decades later.

Widely credited as the principal architect of India's nuclear energy program, Bhabha died in the 1966 Air India Flight 101 crash near Mont Blanc - but the institutions he built outlasted him by decades.

TIFR and India's nuclear program both trace back to a single engineering student who changed his mind about physics - proof that foundational infrastructure often starts as one person's redirected curiosity.
